newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Airbus says A3XX sales talks continue.
newsitem.headline: Airbus says A3XX sales talks continue.

text.p: Airbus Industrie said it is continuing to talk with potential customers including Singapore Airlines and Japan Airlines for its planned new A3XX aircraft.
This was disclosed in a news briefing here to launch the company's Asia-Pacific market forecast to 2016 by senior vice-president commercial, John Leahy.
Airbus has said that it is currently seeking partners to bear 40 percent of the estimated US$8billion development costs for the all-new 555-seat, double-decker plane.
The first version, the A3XX-100, is scheduled to be launched in December next year for introduction into service in 2003. Cost per aircraft is currently estimated at US$198 million
Leahy said on March 6 that Federal Express was interested in acquiring 10 freighter versions of the A3XX, which would be able to carry more than 130 tonnes of cargo.
During the Hong Kong briefing, he said that the pan-European manufacturer's cargo sales efforts would be concentrated on the new A300-600 freighter aircraft, which are operated by FedEx.
But he stressed that used A300 and A310 former passenger aircraft also offered potential in future freighter configuration.
"As the A300B4 is being retired from passenger service by a lot of airlines, we have enormous interest in turning it into a freight aircfaft," Leahy said.

DHL Airways, U.S. operating unit of DHL Worldwide Express, announced on April 9 that it had signed a memorandum of understanding to buy seven General Electric Co -powered A400B4s for conversion into freighters.

Airbus is a consortium of Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, of France, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler Benz AG, of Germany, British Aerospace and Spain's Construcciones Aeronauticas SA.
